documents.title: Developing course policies around A.I.
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance for writing a syllabus AI policy, noting the faculty senate requires one. It lists considerations and example wording in three categories plus mixed-use classes.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use' and offers three example categories (permitted, allowed under circumstances, prohibited) rather than setting one rule, so it delegates.

units.why: The faculty senate mandate is a requirement on instructors: it says the senate 'now requires that you incorporate a policy related to AI use into your syllabus', which is P09 (syllabus AI statement), addressed to instructors before the course.
units.anchor: the faculty senate at UNL now requires that you incorporate a policy related to AI

units.why: 'It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use' hands the choice to instructors, so P04, not a university default.
units.anchor: It is entirely up to the individual instructor to determine which policy to use

units.why: The page says there is 'a wide variation in AI policy across the university' (some allow any use, others prohibit entirely); this describes the instructor-by-instructor pattern, P04, as a fact.
units.anchor: Some instructors allow any use of AI in the completion of coursework, while others prohibit

units.anchor: students may assume that the rules from their other courses also apply in yours
